input.query: SELECT service_name, span_name, count(*) n, approx_quantile(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95_ms, avg(duration)/1e6 avg_ms FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY p95_ms DESC LIMIT 30
SELECT service_name, span_name, count(*) n, approx_quantile(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95_ms, avg(duration)/1e6 avg_ms FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY p95_ms DESC LIMIT 30

content.text: The slowdown sits on the `search → geo` call (about 2.9 s, versus 0.58 ms in normal). Next I'll look at geo's own spans and its database spans.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' src, service_name, span_name, count(*) n, approx_quantile(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95_ms, min(duration)/1e6 min_ms, max(duration)/1e6 max_ms, count(DISTINCT attr_status_code) codes FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('geo','mongodb-geo','search') OR span_name LIKE '%geo%' OR span_name LIKE '%mongo%' GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, span_name, count(*), approx_quantile(duration,0.95)/1e6, min(duration)/1e6, max(duration)/1e6, count(DISTINCT attr_status_code) FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('geo','mongodb-geo') OR span_name LIKE '%geo%' OR span_name LIKE '%mongo%' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,1

content.text: Geo's own server spans are fast (0.2 ms p95), but the caller waits 1.4–3.1 s for them. The delay is on the search→geo path, outside geo's processing. Next I'll check logs and metrics for search, geo and frontend to tell network delay from HTTP-layer slowness.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' src, service_name, severity_text, count(*) n, any_value(body) ex FROM abnormal_logs GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, severity_text, count(*), any_value(body) FROM normal_logs GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,1

SELECT 'abn' src, metric_name, count(*) n, count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) pods FROM abnormal_metrics_sum GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', metric_name, count(*), count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) FROM normal_metrics_sum GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2,1

content.text: Logs carry no signal. Next I'll compare metric averages per service between periods, starting with the services the survey flagged.

input.query: WITH a AS (SELECT 'abn' src, service_name, metric, avg(value) v, count(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics GROUP BY 1,2,3), n AS (SELECT 'norm' src, service_name, metric, avg(value) v, count(*) n FROM normal_metrics GROUP BY 1,2,3) SELECT coalesce(a.service_name,n.service_name) svc, coalesce(a.metric,n.metric) m, n.v nv, a.v av, a.n an, n.n nn FROM a FULL OUTER JOIN n ON a.service_name=n.service_name AND a.metric=n.metric WHERE coalesce(a.service_name,n.service_name) IN ('search','geo','frontend','reservation','rate','profile') ORDER BY 1,2

input.query: WITH a AS (SELECT service_name, metric, avg(value) v FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE service_name IN ('search','geo','reservation') GROUP BY 1,2), n AS (SELECT service_name, metric, avg(value) v FROM normal_metrics WHERE service_name IN ('search','geo','reservation') GROUP BY 1,2) SELECT coalesce(a.service_name,n.service_name) svc, coalesce(a.metric,n.metric) m, round(n.v,2) nv, round(a.v,2) av FROM a FULL OUTER JOIN n ON a.service_name=n.service_name AND a.metric=n.metric WHERE abs(coalesce(a.v,0)-coalesce(n.v,0)) > 0.2*abs(coalesce(n.v,0))+1e-9 ORDER BY 1,2

content.text: Reservation's memory RSS jumped from about 13 MB to about 1 GB, which needs its own check. First I'll pin down where the search→geo delay sits: before the request reaches geo, or on the response path. That needs the trace schema.

input.query: WITH j AS (SELECT p.trace_id, p.service_name caller, p.span_name pname, p.duration pdur, p.time ptime, c.service_name callee, c.span_name cname, c.duration cdur, c.time ctime, c.attr_k8s_pod_name cpod, p.attr_k8s_pod_name ppod FROM abnormal_traces p JOIN abnormal_traces c ON c.parent_span_id=p.span_id AND c.trace_id=p.trace_id WHERE p.service_name='search' AND c.service_name='geo') SELECT 'abn' src, count(*) n, approx_quantile(extract(epoch FROM ctime)-extract(epoch FROM ptime),0.5)*1000 start_gap_ms_med, approx_quantile((extract(epoch FROM ptime)+pdur/1e9)-(extract(epoch FROM ctime)+cdur/1e9),0.5)*1000 end_gap_ms_med, approx_quantile(pdur/1e6,0.5) caller_ms, approx_quantile(cdur/1e6,0.5) callee_ms, count(DISTINCT cpod) callee_pods, count(DISTINCT ppod) caller_pods FROM j

content.text: The gap is before the request reaches geo: geo starts about 1.6 s after search and finishes right when search does, so the delay is on the request path only. Next I'll check reservation's memory jump over time, plus restarts and uptime across services.

input.query: SELECT service_name, metric, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, min(time) t0, max(time) t1, count(*) n, min(value) mn, max(value) mx FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('k8s.pod.uptime','k8s.container.restarts','container.memory.rss','container.cpu.usage') AND (service_name IN ('reservation','search','geo','frontend') OR metric LIKE 'k8s.%') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 1,2,3

content.text: Reservation's RSS climbed from 13 MB to about 1 GB with no restarts or new pods. I'll check whether that rise is gradual and whether reservation's latency follows it.

input.query: WITH m AS (SELECT floor(extract(epoch FROM time)/60) b, avg(value)/1e6 rss_mb FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE service_name='reservation' AND metric='container.memory.rss' GROUP BY 1), t AS (SELECT floor(extract(epoch FROM time)/60) b, count(*) n, approx_quantile(duration,0.5)/1e6 p50, approx_quantile(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95 FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='reservation' AND span_name LIKE 'reservation.%' GROUP BY 1) SELECT m.b, round(rss_mb,1) rss_mb, t.n, round(t.p50,2) p50, round(t.p95,2) p95 FROM m LEFT JOIN t USING(b) ORDER BY 1

content.text: Reservation's memory stepped up once at the start of the incident and then stayed flat, while its own latency barely moved. Before deciding on it, I'll compare CPU for the services with the largest CPU shifts (frontend, attractions) to see whether either is a separate fault.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' src, service_name, metric, round(avg(value),4) v, count(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('container.cpu.usage','k8s.pod.cpu.node.utilization') AND service_name IN ('frontend','attractions','search','geo','profile') GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, metric, round(avg(value),4), count(*) FROM normal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('container.cpu.usage','k8s.pod.cpu.node.utilization') AND service_name IN ('frontend','attractions','search','geo','profile') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text:
**Verdict: the evidence supports `network_delay` on the search→geo connection. I'd put confidence at about 0.75.** The one open alternative is a client-side or HTTP-level stall in search that I can't rule out from traces alone.

**What supports it**

- **The wait is outside both ends.** Abnormal search→geo `geo.Geo/Nearby` calls (n=338) have a start gap from the caller's Client span to geo's Server span of p25 1,544 ms, p50 1,594 ms, p95 2,942 ms. Normal p50 was 0.20 ms. Geo's own span stays at 0.14 ms p50, the same as normal (0.12 ms).
- **Every call is delayed by about the same amount.** The p25 moved as much as the p50 and p95, all about 1.5–1.6 s. That is the delay shape. A loss or corruption shape would leave the median near its normal value and move only the tail in roughly 200 ms steps. Here the median itself moved about 1.6 s.
- **Nothing fails.** Error share is 0.00 on the call and on geo. Geo keeps emitting spans and logs, and its call volume falls only in line with search's reduced throughput. That argues against `network_partition`, `network_loss` (equivalence class, same answer), and a pod fault at geo.
- **The fault is confined to this connection.** Search's other outgoing call, `rate.Rate/GetRates`, is unchanged: gap p50 0.25 ms (normal 0.19 ms), caller p50 5.0 ms (normal 0.77 ms, which is the same tail effect as its p95). Search's own Server span is slow only because it waits on geo. This rules out a process-wide fault in search and a fault on the rate path.

**What doesn't separate it cleanly**

- **`http_slow` is not fully excluded.** Search makes only one operation to geo, so I can't compare other routes on the same connection to geo. The gap sits before geo's Server span, which is the transport-side signature, but a stall held in search's gRPC client would look similar.
- **No `hubble_*` per-connection metrics exist in this case**, so I can't confirm at the network level that the connection itself is slow.

The claimed kind fits the telemetry; the one piece the traces cannot confirm is whether the delay happens on the wire or inside search's client for the geo route.
